note: E5 (followup_plans.md): three examples or pieces of evidence the writer supplies, per non-personal dev prompt, written 2026-10-24 before any E5 generation. Facts are kept to well-established ones or the writer's own observations. Appended to the instructions as the writer's own words.

a-argue-start-times: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends middle and high schools start at 8:30 a.m. or later.
In my first-period class half the room is still yawning, and two people fell asleep during a quiz last week.
My school starts at 7:20, so I have to catch the bus at 6:35.
a-history-dust-bowl: Farmers plowed up millions of acres of native prairie grass to plant wheat during the 1910s and 1920s.
A long drought hit the southern Plains in the early 1930s.
On Black Sunday, April 14, 1935, a huge dust storm swept across Oklahoma and Texas.
a-oped-library-sundays: On Saturdays I've counted more than twenty people waiting for the library computers.
My neighbor's kids walk there because they don't have Wi-Fi at home.
The coffee shop downtown kicks people out if they stay more than an hour without buying something.
a-explain-vaccines: White blood cells make antibodies that fit a germ's shape, like a key in a lock.
Some vaccines use a weakened or inactivated germ; others teach the body using just one piece of it.
Memory cells stay in the body, which is why you usually don't get chickenpox twice.
a-ethics-historical-figures: Thomas Jefferson wrote that all men are created equal while enslaving people at Monticello.
Some people at the time already argued that slavery was wrong, so it wasn't only a modern idea.
My history teacher says we should understand people in their time without excusing what they did.
a-cause-teens-work: Three of my friends work at the grocery store to save money for a car.
My cousin works because his family needs help paying rent.
One friend's grades dropped when she started closing shifts on school nights.
a-argue-phone-ban: Our school uses phones for the online attendance check-in and some quizzes.
My parents text me if pickup plans change.
In one class the teacher has a phone pocket chart by the door, and people mostly use it.
q-argument-4: College football and basketball bring in a lot of TV money for big schools.
Since 2021 college athletes have been allowed to earn money from their name, image and likeness.
My cousin plays Division I volleyball and has practice, lifting and film for about 30 hours a week.
q-letter-1: There are no crossing guards on Maple between 8 and 8:30 a.m., when most kids arrive.
Cars park on both sides of Maple, so kids step out between them where drivers can't see them.
Last month a car braked hard about two feet from a second grader near the school gate.
q-position-4: Many apps already say users must be 13 or older, but signing up only asks for a birthday.
Some proposals would make people upload a photo ID to prove their age.
My little brother made an account at 10 by typing a fake birth year.
